19 Christmas Dinner Ideas: Main Dishes for the Big Day

Katie Shaw Published:October 13, 2026October 14, 2026 Updated:October 14, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread

Don’t let a morning full of presents have all the fun. Christmas dinner is one of the year’s most special meals. You get to pull out all the stops and make something you’d never make on a weeknight. Here’s a collection of special-occasion faves, with a few picky eater choices thrown in there too.

Apple Cider Glazed Ham

This is the most requested Christmas main dish at my house. It’s kid-friendly, not too sweet, glazed to perfection, and gorgeous on the table.

Get the Recipe

Prime Rib Roast

A classic and hearty recipe that will keep the house smelling amazing all evening. Check with your local butcher first, as you may need to order the roast ahead of time (especially around the holidays).

Get the Recipe

Deep-Fried Turkey

Beautifully browned crispy skin wirh moist, flavorful meat. Say goodbye to boring turkey with this delicious recipe. You'll never make turkey another way.

0

Get the Recipe

Pork Tenderloin

This recipe can be made right in a cast iron skillet. It’s quick and easy. Drizzle with the honey balsamic glaze, and it’s a simple, fancy Christmas dinner.

Get the Recipe

Roast Chicken

Cast iron chicken is great for a smaller crowd and when you don’t want to fuss with a whole roast or turkey. You can pair it with just about any side dish.

Get the Recipe

Roast Beef and Yorkshire Pudding

A timeless classic for when you’re really feeling like going old-fashioned. This recipe alone is enough for the table, so you don’t need to go crazy over the sides.

Get the Recipe

Beef Wellington

Most of the work is done ahead of time for this recipe. (But it does require some work.) It’s well worth it, though. This dish is a true showstopper if you want to wow your guests.

Get the Recipe

Crown Roast of Pork

Another dish that will really impress your friends and family. I like this as an alternative to turkey (because we just did that for Thanksgiving!). Ask your butcher to tie it up for you ahead of time to save you the hassle.

Get the Recipe

Rack of Lamb

The lamb roasts in under half an hour – can you believe it?! This is perfect for a smaller crowd. It’s way easier than it looks and is an easy way to mix up the menu a bit.

Get the Recipe

Roast Duck

If you’re really looking for something that’s different but still easy, try this recipe. It’s not hard, I promise, and duck is a great alternative to chicken or turkey.

Get the Recipe

Beef Bourguignon

Beef bourguignon for when you really don’t want to cook on the big day. You can make this the day before and heat it up before serving. It’s perfect for a cozy and snowy Christmas evening.

Get the Recipe

Roasted Pork Loin

This pork loin cooks in one pan in the oven with apples on top that basically turn into a sauce. It’s a family-friendly recipe that can come together quickly without a lot of hands-on prep.

Get the Recipe

Ossobuco Milanese

For when you’re feeling like Italian, but don’t want fish or pasta. This is a low-and-slow recipe that requires some TLC, but it’s worth it.

Get the Recipe

Roast Beef Tenderloin

I love to make beef tenderloin when I don’t want to fuss with a roast but still want some red meat on the table. The sauce is made from the pan gravy, to keep things simple. It’s leaner and less fatty than a big roast.

Get the Recipe

Smothered Chicken

This is for when things have slowed down, and you’ve been running around to other people’s houses all day. Pair it with simple mashed potatoes and rolls, and you’ve got the ultimate cozy Christmas dinner.

Get the Recipe

Pork Chops with Apples

This slow cooker recipe is perfect when you want a completely hands-off Christmas afternoon. It’s a crowd-pleaser and is great for picky eaters.

Get the Recipe

Tuscan Chicken

This is a one-skillet recipe for when you’re truly tired of the standard holiday fare. There are never any complaints when I make this meal, and you can dress it up with homemade rolls and a roasted vegetable.

Get the Recipe

Beef Brisket

Beef brisket is more affordable than a prime rib roast, plus it’s great for feeding a large crowd.

Get the Recipe

Cast Iron Skillet Chicken Breast

It can never hurt to make some extra chicken for the kids or non-beef eaters. This recipe is super simple and tastes great with whatever sides you’re already making.
